Contrite

/kun-TRYT/ - rhymes with delight · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Contrite means penitent, eager to be forgiven.

Contrite after forgetting the anniversary, Malik cooked her favorite dinner and admitted he had no excuse worth offering.

Worked Example

The batter whose foul ball shattered the bakery window came back that evening contrite: he apologized to the owner face to face, paid for the glass out of his allowance, and swept up every splinter himself.

Contrite goes beyond 'sorry.' A sorry person may just want the moment over; a contrite one genuinely aches over the wrong and wants to be forgiven — the word's root picture is of a heart ground down by what it did.

How Contrite Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

remorseful

remorseful: feels the sorrow for the wrong; contrite adds the eagerness to be forgiven

apologetic

apologetic: says the sorry words, sometimes only out of politeness

Antonyms

unrepentant

unrepentant: refuses to regret the deed

unashamed

unashamed: feels no embarrassment, let alone remorse

How Strong Is It? — sheepish → apologetic → contrite

sheepish vs. contrite

sheepish vs. contrite: Sheepish is much milder than contrite — an embarrassed grin over a small blunder, gone within the minute.

apologetic vs. contrite

apologetic vs. contrite: Apologetic is weaker than contrite — an apologetic person says the right words, while a contrite one genuinely aches to be forgiven.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: thoroughly

Root — trite

Root — trite: rubbed, ground down (Latin terere, tritus)

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (thoroughly) + trite (ground down) = thoroughly ground down. The image is of a heart worn to powder by regret: medieval writers spoke of a 'contrite heart' as one crushed under the weight of its own wrong, which is why contrite still means remorse you can see.

Use the root in a new word: attrition

Use the root in a new word: attrition: The general avoided open battles, preferring a war of attrition that slowly ground the enemy's supplies away.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral to formal

Contrite is for visible, heartfelt remorse that seeks forgiveness right now — the contrite note, the contrite apology at the door. Its unit-mate penitent runs deeper and longer: a penitent person turns sorrow into amends over time, often with a religious echo. If the sorrow is a moment, call it contrite; if it is a path, call it penitent.
